name: Jimi Hendrix
blurb: Redefined what an electric guitar could do with feedback, distortion and sheer volume. His sound is a direct ancestor of heavy metal guitar.

name: Led Zeppelin
blurb: Blueprint for hard rock and heavy metal: crushing riffs, thunderous drums and a mythic stage presence. They disbanded after drummer John Bonham's death in 1980.

name: The Stooges
blurb: Raw, abrasive proto-punk that prefigured both punk and the rawer edges of metal. Iggy Pop's confrontational stage act became a template.

name: Black Sabbath
blurb: Their dark, down-tuned, doom-laden sound is widely regarded as the birth of heavy metal. Almost every later metal subgenre traces back to Tony Iommi's riffs.

name: The Who
blurb: Pioneers of loud, aggressive power-chord rock and the guitar-smashing stage show. Their volume and rock-opera ambition shaped hard rock.

name: David Bowie
blurb: Glam-era shape-shifter whose Ziggy Stardust persona influenced the theatrical side of rock and metal. He also produced and championed the Stooges.

name: AC/DC
blurb: Stripped-down, blues-based hard rock built on Angus Young's riffs and showmanship. Back in Black is one of the best-selling albums ever made.

name: Judas Priest
blurb: Defined the leather-and-studs look and the twin-guitar sound of heavy metal. Their lean, fast approach shaped both NWOBHM and thrash.

name: Ramones
origin: Forest Hills, Queens, New York, USA
blurb: Fast, minimal, three-chord songs that kicked off punk rock. Their speed and brevity fed straight into thrash metal's DNA.

name: Motörhead
blurb: Lemmy's band fused punk speed and metal heaviness before the term crossover existed. A direct influence on thrash and speed metal.

name: Sex Pistols
blurb: Brought punk to the British mainstream with notoriety and one studio album. Their short-lived rebellion shook rock's establishment.

name: Van Halen
blurb: Eddie Van Halen's two-handed tapping and virtuosity raised the bar for rock and metal guitar. They made flashy technique a mainstream ideal.

name: Saxon
blurb: One of the bands most closely identified with the New Wave of British Heavy Metal. Their working-class anthems found a huge audience.

name: Iron Maiden
blurb: The flagship band of the NWOBHM, mixing galloping rhythms, twin-guitar harmonies and epic storytelling. One of metal's biggest touring acts.

name: Misfits
blurb: Horror-punk pioneers whose imagery and melodic hardcore influenced Metallica, Slayer and many others. Metallica later covered their songs.

name: Ozzy Osbourne
blurb: Sabbath's original singer rebuilt his career as a solo star, with Randy Rhoads' neo-classical playing at the front. A defining figure of 1980s metal.

name: Mötley Crüe
blurb: Leading band of the Sunset Strip glam-metal scene. Their image and platinum albums made hard rock a 1980s MTV staple.

name: Venom
blurb: Raw, Satanic-themed and deliberately extreme, they gave black metal its name. A huge influence on thrash, death and black metal.

name: Metallica
blurb: Took thrash from the underground to arenas. Their 1983-1988 run of albums defined the genre.

name: Slayer
blurb: The darkest and fastest of the Big Four. Reign in Blood set a benchmark for extreme metal.

name: Anthrax
blurb: Bridged thrash with humor and hardcore, and later crossed over with rap. Part of the Big Four.

name: Megadeth
blurb: Dave Mustaine's technical, aggressive answer to his old band. Part of the Big Four.

name: Exodus
blurb: Bay Area thrash pioneers and an incubator for Kirk Hammett. Bonded by Blood is a genre classic.

name: Death
blurb: Chuck Schuldiner's band is often called the founder of death metal and evolved toward progressive complexity.

name: S.O.D.
blurb: Stormtroopers of Death mixed thrash with hardcore and dark humor. Speak English or Die helped invent crossover.

name: Possessed
origin: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
blurb: Jeff Becerra's band helped give death metal its name and sound. Seven Churches is a foundational album.

name: Sepultura
blurb: Brazil's thrash and death metal giants brought extreme metal to a global audience.

name: The Exploited
blurb: Loud, aggressive Scottish punk that helped build the crossover between punk and metal.

name: Deep Purple
blurb: Alongside Sabbath and Zeppelin, one of the pioneers of hard rock and heavy metal, with Ritchie Blackmore's riffs and organ-driven power.

name: Hawkwind
blurb: Space-rock pioneers, and the band Lemmy played bass for before founding Motörhead.

name: Raven
blurb: Fast, high-energy NWOBHM band who toured with early Metallica and influenced American speed and thrash metal.

name: Diamond Head
blurb: NWOBHM band whose riffs deeply influenced Metallica, who covered several of their songs.

name: Discharge
blurb: Created the fast, relentless d-beat style that shaped crust, grindcore and thrash.

name: Mercyful Fate
blurb: King Diamond's falsetto and occult imagery, plus intricate twin-guitar writing, influenced thrash and black metal.

name: Overkill
blurb: East Coast thrash stalwarts with a long career built on relentless intensity.

name: Dark Angel
blurb: Technical, brutal thrash from California. Darkness Descends set a high bar for speed.

name: Testament
blurb: Bay Area thrash band, formed as Legacy, whose melodic leads and Chuck Billy's vocals kept them in the first rank.

name: Kreator
blurb: One of the German thrash trio. Pleasure to Kill helped lay foundations for death metal.

name: Celtic Frost
blurb: Evolved from Hellhammer into one of extreme metal's most innovative bands, pushing into avant-garde territory.

name: Bathory
blurb: Quorthon's one-man project is regarded as a forefather of black metal and later Viking metal.

name: Pantera
blurb: Reinvented themselves as a groove-heavy metal band with Cowboys from Hell and became 1990s metal's biggest act.

name: Cream
blurb: Clapton, Bruce and Baker pioneered the loud, improvisational power-trio format that Hendrix, Zeppelin and later heavy bands built on.

name: Blue Cheer
blurb: Played so loud and distorted that their 1968 cover of 'Summertime Blues' is often named as an early heavy-metal record.

name: MC5
blurb: Detroit's high-energy, politically charged rock band, a close cousin of the Stooges and a punk forerunner.

name: Alice Cooper
blurb: Brought theatrical shock-rock to hard rock, with a stage show of gore and horror that heavy metal acts later borrowed.

name: Budgie
blurb: A Welsh power trio whose heavy riffing and sudden dynamics influenced Metallica and Iron Maiden, who both covered their songs.

name: Thin Lizzy
blurb: Their twin-lead-guitar harmonies, pioneered by Scott Gorham and Brian Robertson, became a hallmark of NWOBHM bands such as Iron Maiden.

name: UFO
blurb: Their 1970s records, with Michael Schenker's guitar, were a major influence on the NWOBHM and on Iron Maiden and Metallica.

name: Rainbow
blurb: Ritchie Blackmore's post-Deep Purple band mixed classical-flavored riffs with fantasy lyrics, a template for power and neo-classical metal.

name: Scorpions
blurb: Germany's biggest metal export, they conquered America in the early 1980s with melodic hard rock and metal.

name: Rush
blurb: Canadian trio whose technical prowess and long-form compositions inspired generations of progressive and thrash musicians.

name: Kiss
blurb: Their makeup, pyrotechnics and merchandising turned hard rock into a stadium spectacle, and inspired much of the 1980s image of metal.

name: Blue Öyster Cult
blurb: Intelligent, occult-tinged hard rock that fed into Sabbath-style metal's dark imagery and later thrash cover choices.

name: Uriah Heep
blurb: Organ-driven, gothic-tinged heavy rock with big vocal harmonies, one of the early 1970s' leading heavy bands.

name: Angel Witch
blurb: Their 1980 debut and title track are NWOBHM classics, covered by Metallica and others.

name: Tygers of Pan Tang
blurb: A first-wave NWOBHM band that brought a young Jess Cox and John Sykes into the 1980 scene.

name: Tank
blurb: Algy Ward's Motörhead-influenced NWOBHM band, with the raw 1982 albums Filth Hounds of Hades and Power of the Hunter.

name: Girlschool
blurb: An all-female NWOBHM group who toured and recorded with Motörhead.

name: Def Leppard
blurb: Started in the NWOBHM and became one of the biggest bands of the 1980s with polished, melodic hard rock.

name: Accept
blurb: German heavy metal pioneers whose staccato riffs and gang vocals influenced thrash and power metal.

name: Dio
blurb: Ronnie James Dio's solo band, formed after leaving Black Sabbath, gave 1980s fantasy metal some of its biggest records.

name: King Diamond
blurb: The Mercyful Fate singer's solo project turned horror stories into theatrical concept albums.

name: Manowar
blurb: Loud, bombastic and proudly 'true' heavy metal, with Joey DeMaio's bass and Eric Adams's vocals.

name: Exciter
blurb: Early Canadian speed metal band; Heavy Metal Maniac (1983) was a template for speed and thrash.

name: Anvil
blurb: Fast, raw Canadian metal whose early albums influenced Metallica, Slayer and Anthrax.

name: Metal Church
blurb: Their 1984 debut was among the first American power/thrash records and Elektra's early metal signing.

name: Helloween
blurb: Their Keeper of the Seven Keys albums defined power metal's fast, melodic style.

name: Guns N' Roses
blurb: Raw hard rock that outsold glam metal and helped end the Sunset Strip era.

name: G.B.H.
blurb: British hardcore punks whose fast, distorted sound was popular with early thrash fans.

name: Black Flag
blurb: Pioneers of American hardcore whose relentless touring and heavy sound crossed into metal circles.

name: Dead Kennedys
blurb: Jello Biafra's satirical hardcore band was a central voice of American punk, with songs often covered by thrash bands.

name: Bad Brains
blurb: Black hardcore punk pioneers with extreme speed and technical skill, admired by metal and punk bands alike.

name: Minor Threat
blurb: Their short, fast hardcore songs and straight edge ethos were widely imitated.

name: Suicidal Tendencies
blurb: Venice hardcore punks who became a crossover act, bridging skate punk and thrash metal.

name: D.R.I.
blurb: Dirty Rotten Imbeciles' Crossover (1987) lent its name to the genre blending hardcore and thrash.

name: Corrosion of Conformity
blurb: A hardcore band that moved toward heavy metal and Southern rock by the 1990s.

name: Cro-Mags
blurb: New York hardcore band whose heavy, metallic riffs shaped the metal-hardcore crossover.

name: Agnostic Front
blurb: The leading New York hardcore band, an early cross-over between the genres.

name: Hellhammer
blurb: Crude, murky and deliberately primitive, Hellhammer became one of the roots of black and death metal before evolving into Celtic Frost.

name: Sodom
blurb: One of the German thrash trio, with raw, Venom-influenced early records.

name: Destruction
blurb: German thrash with a relentless, high-speed style led by Schmier.

name: Death Angel
blurb: Bay Area thrash band of Filipino-American cousins whose debut was made when they were teenagers.

name: Nuclear Assault
blurb: East Coast thrash with a mix of humor and politics from ex-Anthrax bassist Dan Lilker.

name: Voivod
blurb: Canadian thrash band that moved into progressive and science-fiction themes.

name: Flotsam and Jetsam
blurb: Phoenix thrash band, best known as the original home of Jason Newsted.

name: Forbidden
origin: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
blurb: Bay Area technical thrash band of the late-80s second wave.

name: Vio-lence
origin: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
blurb: Bay Area second-wave thrash whose singer Sean Killian and guitarist Phil Demmel later influenced the scene.

name: Heathen
blurb: Bay Area thrash with a melodic, technical side.

name: Sacred Reich
blurb: Phoenix thrash with socially conscious lyrics.

name: Annihilator
blurb: Jeff Waters' Canadian band, known for technical thrash with melody.

name: Coroner
blurb: Swiss technical thrash trio with progressive leanings.

name: Tankard
blurb: German thrash band known for beer-themed humor.

name: Onslaught
blurb: One of Britain's earliest and best thrash bands.

name: Sabbat
blurb: British thrash with fantasy and witchcraft themes.

name: Artillery
blurb: Danish thrash band with a technical, European edge.

name: Razor
blurb: Canadian speed/thrash band, famed for its fast, raw sound.

name: Whiplash
blurb: Jersey thrash, inspired by early Slayer and Venom.

name: Morbid Angel
blurb: Their technical, dark death metal, starting with Altars of Madness, helped define the Florida sound.

name: Napalm Death
blurb: Their ultra-fast, short songs founded grindcore and made them a regular on John Peel's show.

name: Obituary
blurb: Their slow, groove-driven death metal, with John Tardy's distinctive voice, was one of the Florida scene's biggest sounds.

name: Carcass
blurb: Grindcore band that moved into melodic death metal with Heartwork.

name: Entombed
blurb: Their 1990 debut Left Hand Path defined the Swedish death metal sound.

name: Deicide
blurb: Controversial Florida band known for blasphemous lyrics and fast, technical death metal.

name: Autopsy
blurb: Their slow, gory, doom-inflected death metal was a landmark of the genre.

name: Cannibal Corpse
blurb: Brutal death metal pioneers with graphic lyrics, long a top-selling extreme metal band.

name: Bolt Thrower
blurb: Warhammer-themed British death metal with heavy, mid-paced riffs.

name: Atheist
blurb: Technical death metal pioneers with jazz influences.

name: Sarcófago
blurb: Their 1987 debut I.N.R.I. was a notably extreme Brazilian record.

name: Mayhem
blurb: One of the first Norwegian black metal bands, central to the genre's second wave.

name: Repulsion
blurb: Their Horrified is an early grindcore and death metal landmark.

name: Terrorizer
blurb: World Downfall (1989) is a landmark of American grindcore and death metal.
